chapter: Brother Lorenzo Tio Jr. and his career
title: Lorenzo Jr. offered a bandmaster post in the Eighth Illinois band
summary: In the First World War draft period Lorenzo Jr. in Chicago was wanted as a bandmaster for his transposition skill on a single B-flat clarinet, but he returned home because his wife was expecting.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: And, uh, during the First World War, he was, uh, my brother left from here and went to Chicago. And, uh, during the draft, they wanted him, uh, went on the rehearsal with the Bay, Illinois, and they, uh, wanted him as a bandwriters. Because he knew this transposition business to and fro. He could take a B flat tire and make a monkey with that.

And, uh, that you wanted, he didn't have to use from the A, C, E, or B flat. All he wanted was that B flat. And he could pull it out to make any tone that you want out of it. Because he was a fellow, he didn't believe in carrying a whole lot of instrument with him. Do you know that?
Yeah, he'd take that B flat clarinet and play any part or any key, you know, like, it was just a key or something.

I remember once Bunk Johnson told me that he came to the, he didn't, wasn't a regular member of the Eagle Band, but one day he went there to play with the Eagle Band, and they said, what's the matter, you only have your one clarinet. He said, I think I can do it all right. That's right. And he didn't need all those others.

So he didn't need all of them, you see. So, uh, that made him kind of a thing, because Dully wanted him to be a bandwriters in the Eagle, Illinois, but then he, he didn't care about that because he wasn't married and his wife was about to have a child. And he even figured I was going in the army, so he decided he'd come back here again. And also he'd written a lot of numbers.
